html:
Jesus of Nazareth was a Jewish preacher from Galilee who lived from about 6 to 4 BCE until about 30 CE, and whose life and death are the centre of Christianity, the largest religion in the world. He lived in a land ruled by the Roman Empire and its client kings.

Nearly all historians agree that he was a real person. Almost everything we know about him comes from the four gospels of the New Testament, written some decades after his death, with brief mentions by the Jewish historian Josephus and the Roman historian Tacitus.

What the sources say he did:

  • He was baptised by John the Baptist, a prophet who called people to repent.
  • He gathered followers, including twelve disciples, and travelled around Galilee teaching about the coming kingdom of God, often in parables.
  • He became known as a healer, and ate with outcasts and people seen as sinners.

Around 30 CE he went to Jerusalem for the Passover festival. He was arrested, handed over to the Roman governor Pontius Pilate and executed by crucifixion. His followers said that he rose from the dead and appeared to them, and that he was the Messiah, or Christ.

At first his followers were a small group within Judaism. Missionaries such as Paul took the message to non-Jews across the Roman world, and within three centuries Christianity became the religion of the emperors. Islam also honours Jesus, as a prophet and the Messiah, though not as the son of God. The common Western calendar counts years from the estimated year of his birth.
